claims.text: As-synthesized CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles have a uniform elemental distribution.
High-temperature degradation of CoCrFeNiMn nanoalloys is primarily initiated by oxygen ingress.
Enhanced surface diffusion facilitates oxygen ingress into CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles at high temperature.
Oxygen ingress causes early surface oxidation.
Oxidation triggers elemental segregation in CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles.
Oxidation triggers phase decomposition in CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles.
An intact, defect-free ALD alumina coating acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Limiting oxygen penetration with an alumina coating retards surface oxidation.
Retarding oxidation with an alumina coating suppresses associated chemical and structural destabilization.
After exposure at 700°C for 3 hours in an oxidizing atmosphere, coated nanoparticles will show less oxidation than uncoated nanoparticles.
After the specified exposure, coated nanoparticles will show negligible elemental segregation relative to uncoated nanoparticles.
After the specified exposure, coated nanoparticles will largely retain their homogeneous phase structure.
Uncoated nanoparticles will exhibit measurable surface oxidation after exposure at 700°C for 3 hours in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Uncoated nanoparticles will exhibit the onset of phase decomposition under the specified exposure.
The alumina barrier may become less effective at substantially higher temperatures or longer exposure times.
Interfacial defects or reactions could compromise the alumina coating's barrier function.

contradictions.description: The prediction is explicitly conditional on the coating remaining conformal and defect-free, but the falsification rule treats observation of a non-uniform or compromised coating as falsification. Coating failure violates the hypothesis's stated boundary rather than decisively testing whether an intact coating is an effective barrier.
